title: 2004 HMMT February Guts Problem 26
statement: How many of the integers \(1,2, \ldots, 2004\) can be represented as \((m n+1) /(m+n)\) for positive integers \(m\) and \(n\) ?

solutions.text:
2004
For any positive integer \(a\), we can let \(m=a^{2}+a-1, n=a+1\) to see that every positive integer has this property, so the answer is 2004.
